title: Keyproof Collector: unified KMS/HSM evidence aggregation and rotation audit
creator: Ava Brooks
description: Build a lightweight, vendor-agnostic service (Keyproof Collector) that continuously gathers cryptographic evidence from KMS and HSM integrations across Redwood deployments (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). The service will produce verifiable artifacts for rotation events, key provenance, wrapping/unwrapping operations, and proof-of-residency assertions that feed into automated compliance reports and customer evidence bundles.
goals: Automate collection of key rotation events and signing metadata from AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and partner HSMs
Standardize evidence artifacts (signed JSON bundles + immutable audit index) for retention and export
Expose a read-only API and scheduled report generator for compliance teams and customer requests
Integrate with existing audit pipeline and alerting (link to ENG-12037) and support configurable retention/retention-policy labels per customer/tenant
non_goals: Acting as a key management UI (we will not replace customer KMS key lifecycle workflows)
Implementing new cryptographic primitives — rely on vendor HSM/KMS for signing and attestations
acceptance_criteria: Collector can connect and authenticate to AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault in Redwood staging using service roles and sample tenant configs
Rotation events (create/disable/rotate/destroy) are captured with timestamps, operator identity, and vendor-signed metadata
Artifacts are immutable once written and mapped to tenant IDs with configurable retention and export endpoints
Automated report for a 90-day window can be generated and contains cryptographic proofs suitable for audit review
End-to-end tests for HSM connector mocked vendor responses included in CI
implementation_notes: Design will rely on an append-only audit index stored in an encrypted object store (Immutable S3 prefix / versioned blobstore) with per-tenant encryption keys. For Hosted/Dedicated we'll use service-role integrations; for Private/VPC deployments the agent will run in-customer network and push signed bundles back to a collector endpoint or write to a customer-provided S3/GCS bucket. We will sign the report manifest with a short-lived service cert and include vendor attestation blobs where available.
tradeoffs: Centralized collector simplifies reporting but requires careful multi-tenant isolation and RBAC; alternative is per-tenant collector agents which increases ops surface
Storing evidence centrally improves UX for support but increases responsibility for encrypted retention — mitigated by allowing customer-managed storage option
Relying on vendor attestation avoids re-implementing crypto proofs but means different evidence shapes per vendor; normalize at packaging stage
test_plan: Unit tests for vendor connectors and parsing logic
Integration tests against KMS emulator (localstack / gcp-mock) and HSM emulator where possible
E2E in a staging environment with one Hosted tenant, one Dedicated pool, and a Private deployment agent
Fuzz/negative tests for partial failures (network partition, expired creds) to validate retry/backoff and alerting
rollout_plan: Alpha: run collector in read-only mode for a handful of internal tenants and verify artifacts
Beta: enable for security+enterprise customers behind feature flag with opt-in retention policies
GA: on by default for accounts with compliance package purchased; provide exports and self-service evidence downloads
rollout_blockers: Finalizing HSM vendor SDK legal review (ops/security)
SLA for event delivery from Dedicated pools under heavy load
Decision on default retention policy and encryption key residency for central store
